text:
The Nifty 50 closed at 25,800.6, up 1.12% on the day and 2.61% over the past five sessions, while the broader Nifty 500 rose 0.8% (1.49% five‑day). Advances (247) almost matched declines (243), giving a breadth score of 69.9 in the “HEALTHY” zone, with more than half of stocks above their 200‑day moving average. Bank Nifty outperformed, ending at 64,635.2, up 2.49% (5.9% five‑day), driven by strong PSU and private‑bank buying.

Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net buyers of about ₹10,308 cr today, extending a 17‑day buying streak, while Domestic Institutional Investors (DIIs) sold roughly ₹4,860 cr, marking three consecutive days of net outflows. The options market shows a put‑call ratio (PCR) of 1.67 for Nifty and 1.37 for Bank Nifty, indicating more put (bearish) open interest. The “max‑pain” levels – where the most options would expire worthless – sit at 25,500 for Nifty and 62,500 for Bank Nifty, with expected trading ranges of 25,609‑25,992 and 63,956‑65,314 respectively. Call walls at 26,000 (Nifty) and 66,000 (Bank Nifty) suggest resistance, while put walls at 24,500 and 63,000 act as support.

Watch the 25,657 P pivot and the 25,495 S1 level for Nifty; a break below S1 could test the 25,494 S1 on Bank Nifty. Key headlines to monitor include the RBI’s upcoming variable‑rate repo auction (Nov 23) and any further FII inflows, as the sector quadrants still show “leading” banks and financials. Keep an eye on the India VIX, now at 17.32 (+7.5% today), for signs of rising volatility.
